title: Ruling: safe: hold has no wire form (position actuators)
description: CANON FLAG, DESIGN.md section 15 Q15. Isotope's config gives position actuators safe: hold (stop driving, stay put; DESIGN 5, 10.2). SPEC 8.8 (Valence 9dd395d) makes safe a typed value inside min/max and 13.3.1 item 5 holds every actuating field at it, so a position target's safe value is a position and entering safe drives toward it. Options: (a) RFC for a hold meaning on a command.position field's safe state; (b) remodel the stand as a drive enable (safe false) beside the target. Read: (a) is honest, (b) reports a target the actuator is not seeking.
acceptance_criteria: Operator picks (a) or (b); DESIGN.md 5, 10.2 and Q15 updated in the same commit; for (a), the RFC draft is appended to Valence RFC-QUEUE.md.

title: Ruling: accessory channel budget is hub-advertised, not a fixed 128
description: The 2026-09-26 ruling says up to ~128 channels per accessory. The reference hub's catalog is Catalog32 = BasicCatalog<48, 200, 160, 192, 4> (48 entries, 200 layout fields; Valence lib/valence/include/valence/channel/catalog.hpp:880) and Nucleus already uses 189 of 200 layout fields (flagship_p4/src/hub/ValenceCatalog.h:1691). One 128-channel accessory does not fit; three typical ones may not. Proposal in DESIGN.md section 8: the hub advertises its remaining accessory budget (probe reply and join answer); an accessory that does not fit is refused with a reason and the numbers (SPEC 4.5); 128 is only Isotope's per-declaration ceiling. Separate question: does the Valence catalog capacity grow (a library change, RFC ritual), and to what.
acceptance_criteria: Operator rules: (1) budget is declared and hub-advertised, yes/no; (2) whether and how far the Valence catalog capacity grows; (3) the id range. DESIGN.md section 8 and Q3 updated in the same commit as the ruling; the Accessory join and declaration RFC carries the budget field.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-10-01 (operator): budget declared and hub-advertised (RFC-077, Valence 4c0ede7: accessories-roster capacity tail, JOIN_REPLY capacity, NACK ACCESSORY_CAPACITY); catalog capacity a hub build parameter (RFC-077 item 8); id range = user space 0x8000-0xBFFF in 32-id slices, 30 own channels (RFC-076, Valence b18fac1; SPEC 8.10). DESIGN.md section 8 and Q3 updated in Isotope bf6af0c.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: ANSWERED by the Valence RFC rulings 2026-10-01 (operator): (1) budget declared and hub-advertised: YES (RFC-077 rfc-cou: capacity on the accessories roster, JOIN_REPLY capacity, NACK ACCESSORY_CAPACITY); (2) the Valence catalog capacity becomes a build-time parameter of the hub (RFC-077 item 8, 'break it now, before any tag'), Flagship sized for its accessory count; (3) id range: user space 0x8000-0xBFFF in 32-id slices (RFC-076 rfc-7bq: r=0 session-scoped, r=1 accessory-status, r=2..31 own, 30 channels max, 512 slices never reused). 128 per accessory is withdrawn as excessive. DESIGN.md section 8 and Q3 updates ride iso-3ph.8; Nucleus halves are val-9u0.19 and val-9u0.20. Ready to close with the ruling stamp.

title: Isotope v0: validate before building
description: Measure every radio number the Isotope design (docs/DESIGN.md) depends on, on dev boards the operator already has (no Flagship PCB yet). Nothing in the implementation epics starts until its blocking validations report. Each child names the number it must produce; results are quoted onto the child, stamped per C-4, with raw captures under artifacts/.
acceptance_criteria: Every child closed with its number stamped on the bead; DESIGN.md open questions Q1, Q5, Q12 and the peer-ceiling line in section 3 updated from the measurements (or flagged if a number contradicts a ruling).

title: Ruling: hub crash-reboot inside the accessory deadman window
description: DESIGN.md section 15 Q16. SPEC 13.3.2 says a host reboot needs nothing extra because every accessory's deadman fires; a crash-reboot shorter than spoke_deadman_ms (or the declared 2 s floor) need not fire it, since the restarted beacon seq is newer or older under 7.3 depending on where the old one stood. The accessory then keeps its last commanded value and never rejoins while the rebooted host has every relationship disarmed (11.6). Proposal: treat a boot_id change from the paired hub as a deadman fire (safe_deadman, rescan, rejoin), and send the case to the Valence queue as an RFC.
acceptance_criteria: Operator rules; DESIGN.md 4/5 and Q16 updated; RFC draft appended to Valence RFC-QUEUE.md if ruled so.

title: RFC-075/078: fold the ruled answers into DESIGN.md (active scan, one clock, channels 1-13, pause via interlock, seven maps, relationships STORE)
description:
RFC-075 (Valence rfc-2lo) ACCEPTED as drafted and RFC-078 (rfc-j5f) ACCEPTED with the map table, operator rulings 2026-10-01 (comments 01:32). RFC-079 (rfc-ewm, 01:11) and RFC-085 (rfc-crn) touch the same sections.

Answers to write into docs/DESIGN.md:
- Section 6 / Q1: ACTIVE scan (DISCOVER_PROBE); scan channels 1 to 13 everywhere, a regional accessory may subset. iso-3ph.2 still measures it.
- Section 5 / Q5: unicast does NOT refresh the deadman: one clock, the beacon (5 s without beacon, GOODBYE, or any ESTOP = safe state).
- Section 4 / Q2: no STOP bit on the beacon; only estop_latched is broadcast (yes, a latched e-stop puts every accessory safe). Under RFC-085 pause reaches accessories through the RFC-078 interlock as commanded safe values.
- Section 7 / Q7: one join per window; a configure session may open the window in-band; pairing waits until the hub has joined WiFi (RFC-079).
- Section 9 / Q8: relationships are authored through RFC-067 store verbs (a relationships STORE with action.store, store_id per RFC-070); relationship-admin dropped; maps 1 linear_clamp, 2 invert, 3 threshold_hysteresis, 4 slew_limit, 5 lowpass, 6 gate, 7 piecewise_table, parameters in physical units; chains allowed, loops rejected at put; pause disarms; direct client writes under pause allowed; stream stamps applied on arrival, no spoke time sync.
- Section 15 Q0: config mode is BLE + USB serial, no WiFi, no softAP (RFC-079); the hardware SPEC row is the Hardware repo's to amend.
- Section 14: mark RFC-075..079 accepted with dates.

Prove it: canon_lint zero findings; every answered question in section 15 carries the ruling date and RFC id; no section still says 'proposal' for a ruled item.
close_reason: Landed answers written into DESIGN.md against Valence 9dd395d: header and section 2 (spec now gives the spoke), 3 (no softAP, SPEC 13.3.1 item 9/13.4.1), 4 (BEACON payload as pinned, beacon_flags, no PAUSE/STOP bit), 5 (one clock, four safe doors, sticky safe, accessory_states), 6 (active scan, channels 1-13, broadcast probe answer, no spoke in config mode), 7 (JOIN_REQ/JOIN_REPLY as registered, one join per window, in-band window_open, rejoin, random u64 accessory_id), 8 (declaration is a catalog, safe key 25, validation, persistence, proxy, H13 obligations), 9 (seven maps, relationships STORE 0x0013-0x0015 via store verbs, arming is resume, interlock incl. pause), 14 (RFC-075..079 + 085 with landed shas). Section 15: Q0, Q1, Q2, Q5, Q7, Q8 answered with ruling date + RFC + SPEC section; Q4, Q6, Q13 also answered by the landed spec (RFC-076/075). New flags raised: Q15 (safe: hold has no wire form, CANON FLAG) and Q16 (hub crash-reboot inside the deadman window). Lint: codespell en-GB_to_en-US zero findings.

title: RFC-078: accessory firmware implements the accessory conformance profile duty set

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Conformance checklist landed as DESIGN.md section 17 (SPEC 17.1.1 at Valence 9dd395d): 16 duties, each with its proposed owning module (wire, link, scan, join, identity, declaration, intent, channels, stream, safety; generator owns declaration lint), plus the absent-by-profile list. No firmware yet; module split fixed when Q9 (generator shape) is ruled. Bead stays open for the implementation and its Prove-it.

title: RFC-076: recompute the frame budget and DESIGN.md at 32-id slices / 30 channels per accessory
description:
RFC-076 (Valence rfc-7bq) ACCEPTED with the slice narrowed, operator ruling 2026-10-01 (comment 01:32): slice width 32 ids (accessory_slice_ids 0x20): r=0 session-scoped, r=1 accessory-status, r=2..31 the accessory's own (30 channels at most). User space 0x8000-0xBFFF holds 512 slices; a forgotten slice is never reused for the life of a hub. Rationale: pump 3 channels, three-motor vibrator ~6, motorized stand 6-8; a worst-case 30-channel declaration is about 3.5 KB (19 chunks). Also ruled: carve from reserved yes; one join per window; a configure session may open the window in-band; no STORE entries in a declaration; the hub does not rewrite group strings. RFC-077: capacity is hub-advertised (roster, JOIN_REPLY, NACK ACCESSORY_CAPACITY) and the hub's catalog capacity is a build-time parameter.

Change: tools/frame_budget.py worst case moves from 128 actuators to 30 (and 15 mirrored pairs); docs/DESIGN.md section 16 table regenerated from it (bytes, chunks at 192 B, frames at 242 B), section 8 (slice, id range, budget), section 3 (topology numbers), section 15 Q3 answered with the ruling. iso-3ph.7's acceptance ('128-channel declaration') reads 30-channel.

Prove it: tools/frame_budget.py run through the quiet launcher prints a 30-channel worst case near 3.5 KB / 19 chunks (state the exact numbers on close); DESIGN.md section 16 matches the script output byte for byte; canon_lint zero findings.
close_reason: Recomputed at 32-id slices / 30 channels (Valence 9dd395d, SPEC 8.10/13.3.1/13.3.2). tools/frame_budget.py: worst-case declaration 3,592 B (status entry 102 B + 30 x ~117 B, 116.3 B/channel), 19 chunks at 192 B, 15 frames at 242 B, under accessory_declaration_max_bytes 4,096 B; 30 actuators, 30 readouts and 15 mirrored pairs all equal once layout size (key 18) is counted; 3,646 B in the hub catalog (absolute ids), inside Nucleus's 5,120 B per-accessory budget. One 242 B payload holds status + 1 worst-case channel. Hub per accessory, reconciled with Nucleus docs/accessory-store-sizing.md: PSRAM ~14.0 KB (pools 7,612 B + scratch share 6,400 B), flash 8,192 B A/B at the ceiling (7,184 B at worst case). Frames: BEACON 30, JOIN_REQ 60, JOIN_REPLY 26, BLOB_CHUNK 214. DESIGN.md sections 3, 8, 10, 15 Q3, 16 updated; section 16 quotes the script output verbatim. Lint: codespell en-GB_to_en-US zero findings (Isotope names no lint of its own).

title: 250 B frame budget: the beacon and a 128-channel declaration
description: Desk work plus one wire check. Method: encode the DESIGN.md section 4 beacon and a synthetic 128-channel declaration (DESIGN.md section 8 fields at worst case: f32 min/max/safe, key and unit strings at their max) in the proposed layout; count bytes; send both between two dev boards and capture them. Also check whether the broadcast peer counts against the 20-peer limit (add 20 unicast peers plus broadcast; record which add fails). Numbers to produce: beacon bytes on the wire; declaration bytes total and per channel; frame count at 242 B and chunk count at 192 B; accessory ceiling with broadcast added.
acceptance_criteria: Beacon at or under 250 B confirmed on the wire; 128-channel declaration size and chunk count stamped, with the verdict that it rides blob-style chunking (not section 5.6 fragmentation); accessory ceiling (19 or 20) stamped and DESIGN.md section 3 updated.
close_reason: Superseded. The 128-channel declaration is withdrawn by the RFC-076 ruling (Valence b18fac1); the 30-channel paper recompute is iso-3ph.8 (Isotope bf6af0c: 3,592 B, 19 chunks). The broadcast-peer ceiling is now normative: 19 accessories by unicast, SPEC 13.3.1 item 8 (RFC-075, Valence 8484552). The 30 B beacon on the wire rides iso-3ph.1 method (1).

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: PAPER VERDICT 2026-10-01 (tools/frame_budget.py, DESIGN.md §16; encodings per RFC-075 item 3 and RFC-076 item 5 / SPEC Appendix C, §5.3 profile). Beacon: 8+22 = 30 B of 250, fits. BLOB_CHUNK frame: 8+14+192 = 214 B. Worst-case declaration entry (strings at CDDL max, f32 min/max/safe): actuator 117 B, readout 115 B, mirrored pair 232 B, status entry 96 B. 128 actuators: 15,052 B total, 116.8 B/channel, 79 chunks at 192 B, 63 frames at 242 B; RFC-076 legal max 126 ids: 14,818 B, 78 chunks. One frame holds 1 worst-case channel beside the status entry (215 B). Verdict: rides blob-style chunking (ns 0), NOT §5.6 fragmentation. Flags: DESIGN §8's old 26 B/channel estimate was 4.5x low; RFC-076 slice holds 126 own channels not 128 (63 if actuators are mirrored pairs), owned by §15 Q3. STILL OWED (bench): beacon at or under 250 B confirmed on the wire between two dev boards; 20 unicast peers + broadcast add, record which add fails (ceiling 19 vs 20) and update DESIGN §3. Left open: paper verdict landed, bench confirmation owed.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RFC-076 ruling 2026-10-01 narrows the slice to 32 ids / 30 channels (worst case ~3.5 KB, 19 chunks), so the 128-channel declaration in this bead's acceptance is superseded by a 30-channel one; the paper recompute is iso-3ph.8. The beacon number (30 B) and the broadcast-peer ceiling check stand.

title: BLE via esp_hosted on the P4 + C6 pair
description: Same P4 devkit + C6 with the ESPHome co-processor image. Config mode (the Config mode RFC, DESIGN.md section 14) needs the hub to advertise over BLE with the pairing-window flag and accept a GATT connection. Method: bring up the esp_hosted BLE path on the P4 (confirm the ESPHome image keeps the controller exposed), advertise the Valence service UUID (SPEC section 13.4), connect from Phosphor's shell or nRF Connect, exchange writes and notifies. Numbers to produce: does BLE work with the ESPHome image at all (yes/no); negotiated ATT MTU; notify throughput (B/s); connect time (ms).
acceptance_criteria: BLE advertising and a GATT connection proven on the P4 + C6 pair with the ESP-NOW-capable image, MTU and throughput stamped; or the incompatibility named and the image choice flagged for a ruling.

title: Coexistence on the C6: ESP-NOW + station + BLE advertising at once
description: Same P4 + C6 pair running all three: station associated with traffic (a WS client streaming at 30 Hz, or a sustained download), ESP-NOW beacon at 1 Hz plus unicast to one accessory at 50 Hz, BLE advertising (and a separate run with one BLE connection held). Method: each alone, then in pairs, then all three, 10 minutes each. Numbers to produce: ESP-NOW beacon loss and unicast loss/RTT in each combination; station throughput in each; BLE advertising interval actually achieved.
acceptance_criteria: Loss/latency/throughput matrix across the combinations stamped; verdict line on whether all three run together within validation (a)'s deadman false-trip bound, or which one must yield.

title: Channel-scan join time, cold and after a forced router channel change
description: Hub dev board as a station on a router whose channel can be set by hand; accessory dev board already paired (hub id stored). Method: (1) cold: power the accessory 20 times with the hub on channels 1, 6, 11 and 13; measure power-on to first valid hub beacon. Run both scan forms from DESIGN.md section 6: passive listen (dwell 150 ms and 1050 ms) and active probe (a probe frame per channel, the hub answers at once, 150 ms dwell). (2) forced change: with the accessory joined, move the router from channel 1 to 11; measure last beacon on the old channel, deadman trip, first beacon on the new channel. Also record how often a beacon on channel N is heard while tuned to N+1 or N-1 (the reason for the wifi_channel field). Numbers to produce: join time p50/max for each scan form and dwell; total outage after a router channel change; adjacent-channel hear rate.
acceptance_criteria: Join-time table per scan form stamped here, with the verdict for DESIGN.md Q1: does passive listening at 1 Hz meet the ruled ~2 s worst case (expected no, ~13 s) and does the active probe (expected yes)? Router-change outage measured end to end.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: RFC-075 ruling 2026-10-01: ACTIVE scan is ruled, channels 1 to 13 everywhere (a regional accessory may subset). Still measure both forms: the ~2 s worst-case claim and the router-change outage need the numbers.

title: Deadman timing: last beacon to safe state, measured on a pin
description: Accessory dev board drives a GPIO as its actuator (on = high, safe = low). The hub (1) stops beaconing on command, (2) is power-cut, (3) sends a going_away beacon. A scope or logic analyzer captures the hub's beacon TX (a hub GPIO toggled on each send) and the accessory's actuator pin. 30 trials per stop form. Also verify that after beacons return the pin stays safe until a fresh command arrives (safe is sticky). Numbers to produce: time from last beacon to safe edge (expected 5.0 s plus up to one beacon period of phase), its jitter, and time from going_away to safe edge.
acceptance_criteria: Measured last-beacon-to-safe distribution (min/p50/max) and goodbye-to-safe latency stamped here from scope captures; sticky-safe behavior confirmed on 30 of 30 trials, or the failure named.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Stop form (3) is now a broadcast GOODBYE (REBOOTING or NORMAL_CLOSURE), not a going_away beacon bit: SPEC 13.3.1 item 5(b) (RFC-075, Valence 8484552). Also measure ESTOP-to-safe (item 5(c)).

title: esp_hosted CustomRpc ESP-NOW shim on a P4 devkit + C6 (ESPHome co-processor image)
description: ESP32-P4 devkit with its C6 flashed with ESPHome esp-hosted-firmware (the ESP-NOW overlay; its README says esp_hosted >= 2.8.1, its PR #17 says CI defaults to 2.7.0: record the version actually running). Host side: the esphome PR 17712 shim ported to plain ESP-IDF (Nucleus is not ESPHome). Method: esp_now_send from the P4 to a native dev board peer and back, with the C6 also a station on the router. Compare against validation (a)'s native baseline at the same distance: the difference is the SDIO + RPC hop. Then exercise the three defects the PR review recorded: drop a SEND completion (does TX stall forever?), restart the C6 (does the peer mirror go stale?), force a send failure (is it reported?). Never with the P4 in softAP mode. Numbers to produce: added one-way latency of the SDIO hop p50/p99 (ms); max sustained send rate (frames/s); behavior of each of the three defects.
acceptance_criteria: esp_now_send works from the P4 (yes/no, stamped); SDIO hop latency p50/p99 and max send rate stamped; each of the three review defects confirmed or refuted, with the recovery each needs written into the Nucleus-side bead.
notes: The three open review bugs, verbatim from esphome PR 17712 (DESIGN.md section 13 risks): (1) a lost SEND completion permanently stalls TX (no timeout); (2) the host peer mirror is never reconciled after a C6 restart, so peers are never re-added; (3) past 20 peers esp_now_add_peer() returns ESP_OK while the mirror drops the entry, causing a permanent ADD_PEER RPC flood. Test (3) by adding a 21st peer.

title: ESP-NOW range, latency and loss bench (two dev boards)
description: Two ESP32-family dev boards, one as hub, one as accessory. Method: (1) hub broadcasts a 30 B beacon at 1 Hz; accessory logs every seq received. (2) hub unicasts 16 B commands at 1, 10, 50 and 100 Hz; accessory stamps receipt and echoes back; hub measures round trip (one-way = RTT/2, stated as such). Repeat at 1 m, 5 m, 10 m through one interior wall. Repeat every run with the hub board ALSO associated as a station to the house router and a laptop on that AP pulling a sustained download on the same channel. Minimum 10 minutes per cell. Numbers to produce: broadcast beacon loss p (%) per cell; unicast loss (%) after MAC retries; RTT p50/p99 (ms); the implied deadman false-trip interval, about 1/p^5 seconds, per cell.
acceptance_criteria: A table (distance x rate x station traffic on/off) with beacon loss p, unicast loss, RTT p50/p99 and the computed false-trip interval, stamped on this bead. Verdict line: does 5 missed beacons give a false-trip interval above one day in the with-traffic 5 m cell? If not, flag DESIGN.md section 5 for a ruling.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Inherits iso-3ph.7's on-wire check (closed, superseded): confirm the 30 B BEACON (SPEC 13.3.1 item 3, 22 B payload) on the wire in method (1).

title: Isotope visual builder
description: Blueprint-style editor over the config (DESIGN.md section 12). Reads and writes the same config and nothing else. Built last.
acceptance_criteria: A hand-written config round-trips through the builder unchanged in meaning; a config built from scratch in the builder generates and flashes.

title: Hub-side beacon, join, declaration store and relationships (lands in Nucleus)
description: Cross-reference: the work lands in ../Nucleus and must be filed on its board (val- prefix); this bead tracks the dependency from Isotope's side and gets the Nucleus bead id once it exists. Scope: 1 Hz beacon, join window on the pairing button, slice allocation, declaration store (flash, unpacked to PSRAM), live catalog growth, relationships as hub policy, the C6 co-processor image swap, the P4 CustomRpc shim port. Waits on the Valence RFCs named in DESIGN.md section 14. Blocking validations (bd allows only epics to block epics, so the dependency is on iso-3ph as a whole): iso-3ph.1, iso-3ph.3, iso-3ph.4, iso-3ph.5, iso-3ph.6, iso-3ph.7.
acceptance_criteria: The Nucleus bead exists and its id is noted here; an accessory from the generator pairs to Nucleus, its channels appear in the catalog, a relationship driven by machine speed drives it, and it trips safe when Nucleus stops beaconing.
notes: Also waits on ruling iso-yg8 (accessory channel budget); bd lets only epics block epics, so this is noted, not wired.

comments.author: AtlanticTM
comments.text: Nucleus beads exist (2026-10-01): epic val-9u0 with val-9u0.9 (beacon), .10 (pairing window), .11 (join/declaration store), .12 (live catalog growth), .13 (relationship engine), .14 (config mode), .15 (e-stop fan-out), and new from the 2026-10-01 RFC rulings: .17 (wifi_join over BLE + USB serial), .18 (BLE adv layout, no mDNS record), .19 (capacity advertisement), .20 (catalog capacity sizing at 30 channels per slice). Valence library halves: rfc-7n1 (capacity parameter), rfc-58u (live growth).

title: Isotope web flasher
description: A browser page that takes a config, produces the image through the generator, and flashes it over Web Serial (ESP Web Tools shape). Home (this repo or Phosphor) waits on DESIGN.md Q10.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh dev board flashed from the page with each of the three example configs joins a hub and shows its channels in Phosphor.

title: Isotope config format + generator
description: Implement the declarative config (DESIGN.md section 10) with its lint, and the generator that turns it into an image. Shape (compiled vs prebuilt image plus config partition) waits on DESIGN.md Q9. Every wire number comes from the Valence RFCs named in DESIGN.md section 14 once they land; never a local magic number. Blocking validations (bd allows only epics to block epics, so the dependency is on iso-3ph as a whole): iso-3ph.1, iso-3ph.2, iso-3ph.3, iso-3ph.7.
acceptance_criteria: The pump, stand and vibrator configs from DESIGN.md section 10 generate images that boot on the v0 dev boards, declare themselves to a hub, and trip safe within validation (c)'s measured timing. The lint refuses each case listed in section 10.
notes: Also waits on ruling iso-yg8 (accessory channel budget); bd lets only epics block epics, so this is noted, not wired.
